clue.text: Diagnostic expert sacked others to save money

indicators.note: to save is to keep something in, so the rearranged letters hold the currency inside them
sacked suggests something ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the letters of others and to are rearranged

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian unit of money

explanation.surface: An efficiency consultant gets rid of staff to cut costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' reads as fired staff, but it is the anagram signal; 'save' reads as cost-cutting but means keep inside. The money is Russian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called in to find and fix faults in a system is a diagnostic specialist.

clue.text: Fellow's kicked out of splinter group for fighting

indicators.note: kicked out of says one piece is expelled from the group named next

parts.note: a faction is a breakaway group within a party
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, with 's meaning is

explanation.surface: A member is expelled from a breakaway group for brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: Action is combat, as in soldiers seeing action or being killed in action.

clue.text: Make delicate adjustments to beautiful melody

parts.note: fine means beautiful or handsome, as in a fine figure
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A musician polishes a lovely melody with small adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune is to make small precise corrections to something until it works perfectly.

clue.text: Unreliable office worker takes a long time out to lunch

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
an era is a long period of time
out to lunch is slang for crazy, as is mental

explanation.surface: A casual office worker regularly takes extended lunch breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' reads as a long lunch break but is slang for mad, giving MENTAL; 'takes' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperamental machine or person behaves erratically and cannot be depended on.

clue.text: To finish 22 perhaps is a problem

definitions.meaning: 22 is a long-distance phone call, and you end a call by putting down the receiver

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 22 across, a long-distance telephone call; finishing one is putting the phone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a phone call is replacing the receiver; a psychological block is also called by the same phrase as a noun.

clue.text: Lawyer needs time to put down information that's been collected

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
to abase someone is to humiliate or put them down

explanation.surface: A lawyer needs a moment to write down the evidence gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of gathered data held on computer.

clue.text: Fence keeps one in sports ground at all times

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public playing field

indicators.note: in says the next letter sits inside the words that follow it

parts.note: ever means always, at all times
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fence encloses a playing field permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fence is a barrier; the definition is a criminal fence, a receiver of stolen goods. 'keeps' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a fence is someone who buys and sells stolen property, a receiver of stolen goods.

clue.text: What Jacob says about old lady's fruit?

indicators.note: about says the sheep's cry goes round the next piece

parts.note: a Jacob is a breed of sheep, and a sheep says baa
nan is an informal word for grandmother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A question about what a man named Jacob says about his grandmother's fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob looks like a man's name, but it is a breed of spotted sheep, so what it says is BAA.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with yellow skin.

clue.text: So real hardship is represented in collection of poems

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine hardship is depicted in a book of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shropshire Lad is A. E. Housman's 1896 cycle of poems about rural English life; Shropshire is an English county.

clue.text: For schools, term almost has broken up so go from one party to another

definitions.text: go from one party to another

indicators.note: broken up suggests pieces scattered and reassembled, as schools break up at the end of term
almost says the word term loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Schools have broken up for the end of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TERM to TER, which joins FOR SCHOOLS in the anagram signalled by 'has broken up'. Schools breaking up is the British end of a school term.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Commons an MP who changes allegiance to another political party is said to cross the floor.

clue.text: Make one train endlessly on return

indicators.note: on return says the trimmed word is read backwards
endlessly says the word loses both its end letters

parts.note: a train is a retinue, the attendants following an important person

explanation.surface: A train travels without stopping on its way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims RETINUE to ETINU, which 'on return' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join them together into a single whole.

clue.text: A jazz piece is eclipsed by piano and harp playing short passage

indicators.note: eclipsed means hidden behind or surrounded, so these pieces sit inside the following ones

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of harp are performed in a new order

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime music

explanation.surface: A jazz number is overshadowed by piano and harp performing a brief section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipsed' is the container signal: the jazz piece is hidden between piano and the rearranged harp, not after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a short distinct section of a piece of writing.

clue.text: Hungry monkey as it were displaying weariness

indicators.note: as it were flags a whimsical picture: the starving animal has nothing inside it

parts.note: a langur is a long-tailed Asian monkey
a hungry creature has nothing, a zero or letter O, in its belly

explanation.surface: A starving monkey looks listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaying' only links the wordplay to the definition; the trick is reading an empty stomach as a zero placed inside the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a pleasant or lazy tiredness of body or mind.

clue.text: Singer's initial refusal to take on Tosca disheartened another?

indicators.note: initial says only the first letter of singer is used
disheartened says the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: Tosca is an opera by Puccini
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A singer at first declines to take on the role of Tosca.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosca's title role is written for a soprano voice, so the question mark makes 'another' mean another singer of Tosca's kind; 'to take on' attaches the refusal at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca's heroine is a soprano part, so another singer of that kind is a soprano, the highest female voice.

clue.text: Adaptation of Emma's very British but not a byword for ratings?

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks the material, so these letters are rearranged once a is taken away

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter

explanation.surface: A film version of the Jane Austen novel Emma described as very British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a' removes one A from the pool before it is rearranged. Ratings are ordinary sailors in the Royal Navy, whose stock exclamation this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiver my timbers is the stock oath of stage sailors and pirates, so it is a catchphrase of naval ratings.

clue.text: I resign after elected party hides role in crime

indicators.note: after says the following words come after the word for elected

parts.note: a party that is elected is in power
to quit is to resign

indicators.note: hides says a role is hidden away, leaving only what is left of the word party

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A politician quits after their party, once elected, conceals a role in wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' removes PART from PARTY, leaving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An iniquity is a grossly wicked or unjust act, a sin or crime.

clue.text: Karajan, say, turns out Mahler's Sixth very majestically

indicators.note: turns out means expels, so one letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: Herbert von Karajan was a famous conductor, a maestro

indicators.note: Sixth picks the sixth letter of Mahler

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: The conductor Karajan produces a grand performance of Mahler's Sixth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth letter of MAHLER is R, which leaves MAESTRO as MAESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is the Italian musical direction meaning play in a stately, dignified manner.

clue.text: First off, funny fellow's a character

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: comic means funny
Ron is a man's name, a fellow, with 's meaning is

explanation.surface: Right away, a funny man is quite a character.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface character is an eccentric person; the definition is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in writing.

clue.text: Searching question leaves monarch trembling with fear

indicators.note: leaves says the question letters depart and the monarch's letter takes their place

parts.note: quaking means shaking with fear
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: An interrogation leaves the king shaking with fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A raking look or search is one that sweeps thoroughly over everything.

clue.text: Former professors desert institute after termination of tenure

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come after the letter from tenure
termination of picks the last letter of the word tenure

parts.note: a desert is what one deserves, merit

explanation.surface: Retired academics abandon their institution once their tenure ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, as in just deserts, giving MERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti is the plural of emeritus, a retired professor who keeps an honorary title.

clue.text: Purgative obtained from overripe cactus

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A laxative extracted from a cactus that is past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a drug from a South American root used to induce vomiting, an emetic purge.

clue.text: Feature of Elephant and Castle's given everyone a kind of buzz

parts.note: an elephant's most distinctive feature is its trunk
C is an abbreviation for castle, with 's meaning has
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Elephant and Castle, a district of south London, gives everybody a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: Elephant and Castle reads as one London place name, but it splits into two separate pieces. Buzz is slang for a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk call is a dated British term for a long-distance telephone call, and a buzz is a phone call.

clue.text: Police cut is matter for discussion

indicators.note: cut says the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Police budget reductions are a topic for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Keep moving a part of the water pump

definitions.text: a part of the water pump

indicators.note: moving says one letter is shifted to a new place in the word

parts.note: to retain is to keep

explanation.surface: Instructions for keeping a water pump running.
explanation.walkthrough: Water pump is a humorous Chambers term for the eye, which waters when you cry. 'moving' shifts the A in RETAIN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

clue.text: African country somehow wants to import snake? On the contrary

indicators.note: to import is to bring something in, so one piece goes inside the other
on the contrary reverses the roles, so the snake takes the shuffled letters in

parts.note: a boa is a large snake that crushes its prey

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of wants are arranged in some new way

explanation.surface: An African nation apparently wants to bring in snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has 'wants' importing the snake; 'On the contrary' swaps them, so BOA holds TSWAN, the anagram of WANTS made by 'somehow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa.
